# Incident Report: Malware Infection — Host 10.1.21.58 (2026-01-28 capture)

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (NetBIOS alias WIN11OFFICE) |
| AD domain | win11office.com (DC at 10.1.21.2, WIN-LU4L24X3UB7) |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM) |

Confirmed via DHCP Request (frame 1/3, option 12 hostname = DESKTOP-ES9F3ML), NBNS registrations, and Kerberos traffic between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller.

Note: capture file metadata says 2026-01-28 (03:04–03:14 UTC), despite the "2026-01-31" filename/evidence-folder date — traffic timestamps are treated as authoritative below.

## 2. Malware Family / Attribution

**Not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence folder (only the .pcap was supplied), and the actual payload transfer was TLS-encrypted, so no file hash or executable content could be recovered from the wire.

**Behavioral attribution:** the traffic pattern is consistent with a commodity **browser-fingerprinting gate / info-stealer log-upload panel** (the type of infrastructure fronting stealer families such as Lumma/Vidar/Stealc-style loaders), based on:
- A JS payload served over cleartext HTTP that harvests canvas fingerprint, WebGL renderer string, navigator properties, and attempts a WebRTC local-IP leak, then POSTs the JSON blob to `/api/set_agent...&act=log`.
- The gate issues a per-victim `id` + `token` pair reused across the session.
- A leaked internal error string on the site (`GET /favicon.ico` → `cant open archive <public-ip>-<hash>.zip`) shows the backend manages victim data as per-IP zip archives, a pattern typical of stealer log-collection panels.
- A ~16 MB file was pulled from a fake "file hub" download domain immediately before the fingerprinting/C2 traffic began, consistent with delivery of the stealer/loader binary itself (content unrecoverable — TLS).

Treat the family name as **unconfirmed** until the host is imaged and the retrieved binary is hashed/detonated.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

### Command-and-control / tracking endpoints (IP:port)
| Domain | IP | Port | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| whitepepper.su | 153.92.1.49 | 80/tcp, 443/tcp | Primary C2/fingerprint-log gate |
| whooptm.cyou | 62.72.32.156 | 443/tcp | Related gate traffic |
| holiday-forever.cc | 80.97.160.24 | 443/tcp | Related gate traffic |
| communicationfirewall-security.cc | 104.21.9.36 | 443/tcp | Fake "verification" domain, related chain |
| hiyter.com | 104.21.22.231 (Cloudflare) | 443/tcp | Related chain (SNI observed as `cloudflare-ech.com`, domain-fronted) |

### Payload-delivery domains
| Domain | IP(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| arch.filemegahab4.sbs | 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 | ~16 MB downloaded over TLS, 48.4s–70.7s into capture (22s, server→client dominant) |
| media.megafilehub4.lat | 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 | Early-session connection, bidirectional bulk transfer |

### Malicious URLs (captured in full, cleartext HTTP)
```
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log   (POST, fingerprint exfil)
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log
http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico
```

### Victim/session identifiers used against C2
- `id = 3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
- `token = 842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Referenced archive (name only — not directly captured)
- `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip`
- This string was leaked in an HTTP 200 response body from whitepepper.su (an internal "cant open archive ..." error), not an actual file transfer in this pcap. The 32-character hex value is **MD5-length, not SHA256** — no SHA256 of any transferred file is obtainable from this capture, since the only large transfer (the ~16 MB file from arch.filemegahab4.sbs) was TLS-encrypted end to end.

## 4. What Was NOT Found
- No plaintext executable/PE was recoverable via HTTP object export (only JS/HTML fingerprinting payloads and the Windows time-sync/NCSI probes were plaintext).
- Heavy SAMR/LSARPC/DCERPC traffic in the capture is entirely between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2 — normal AD/GPO chatter, not treated as an IOC.
- No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder to cross-check signature hits.

## 5. Recommended Next Steps
1. Image 10.1.21.58 and recover the ~16 MB file fetched from arch.filemegahab4.sbs (48–70s mark) for static/dynamic analysis and hashing.
2. Block/sinkhole all five C2 domains and their resolved IPs at the perimeter.
3. Force credential reset for user `gwyatt` (browser fingerprinting + stealer-style panels commonly precede credential/session-cookie theft).
4. Hunt across the environment for the same `id`/`token` pair or connections to the same five domains from other hosts.
